questions.q: What is the problem with function first(arr: any[]): any { return arr[0]; }?
options: It doesn't compile
It works for every array, but always returns any, losing the specific type information of whatever was passed in
It only works with number arrays
It throws a runtime error on empty arrays
questions.explain: Using any for both the parameter and return type means the function compiles for any array, but every caller gets back an untyped any result regardless of what they passed in.

questions.q: In function first<T>(arr: T[]): T { return arr[0]; }, what does T represent?
options: A specific built-in TypeScript type
A placeholder type, filled in with the actual type used at each call site
A type that must always be explicitly provided by the caller
An error — T is not valid TypeScript syntax
questions.explain: T is a type parameter — a stand-in that TypeScript fills in (usually by inference from the argument) separately for each call.

questions.q: When calling first([1, 2, 3]) where first is the generic version, how does TypeScript determine what T is?
options: You must always write first<number>([1, 2, 3]) explicitly
TypeScript infers T automatically from the argument's type, here number
T defaults to any unless specified
It's a compile error without manual annotation
questions.explain: TypeScript can usually infer the type parameter from the arguments passed, without requiring an explicit <T> annotation at the call site.

questions.q: What does function pair<K, V>(key: K, value: V): [K, V] demonstrate that first<T> does not?
options: That generics can only be used with arrays
That a generic function can declare more than one independent type parameter
That generics are unrelated to type inference
That TypeScript doesn't support tuples
questions.explain: pair has two type parameters, K and V, each inferred independently from its own argument — showing generics aren't limited to a single placeholder.

questions.q: Why would a blockchain library's callContract<T>(method, args): Promise<T> function use a generic return type instead of any?
options: So the caller can specify the exact expected type (like bigint for a balance) and get a correctly typed result back, instead of an untyped any
Because Promise requires a generic parameter to compile at all
Because any is not allowed inside async functions
Generics make the contract call execute faster
questions.explain: A generic return type lets one reusable function still return a precisely typed value per call, which any could never provide.
